name: George Lyttelton, 1st Baron Lyttelton
credit: George Lyttelton, 1st Baron Lyttelton, portrait by an unknown artist, c. 1756 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: George Lyttelton, 1st Baron Lyttelton (1709–1773), was an English politician, patron of James Thomson, Henry Fielding and Alexander Pope, and the author of verse, dialogues and a History of Henry II. He is the Lord Lyttelton of Samuel Johnson's Lives of the Poets.

The poem here is the one printed under his name in Frederick Locker's Lyra Elegantiarum (London: E. Moxon, 1867), an anthology of vers de société and vers d'occasion by deceased authors; the texts follow that first edition.

poems.title: None, without hope, e'er loved the brightest fair
poems.author: George Lyttelton, 1st Baron Lyttelton
poems.collection: Lyra Elegantiarum, ed. Frederick Locker (London: E. Moxon, 1867)
poems.text:
None, without hope, e'er loved the brightest fair,
But love can hope when reason would despair.
